**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE Date Issued: 21</mark>**<sup>**st**</sup> **<mark>September 2010</mark>** 

# **Copper: Preliminary Data for 1**<sup>**st**</sup> **Half 2010** 



The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released preliminary data for June 2010 world copper supply and demand in its September 2010 Copper Bulletin. The Bulletin is available for sale upon request. 

According to preliminary ICSG data, the refined copper market balance for June 2010 indicated a production deficit of 84,000 metric tonnes (t). When making seasonal adjustments for world refined production and usage, June showed a deficit of about 28,000 t. The apparent refined copper balance for the first half of 2010, including revisions to data previously presented, indicates a production deficit of 281,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of 9,000 t). This compares with a production deficit of around 125,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of about 143,000 t) in the first half of 2009. 

World refined copper usage* in June 2010 grew by 12% compared with that in June 2009, mainly owing to the continued recovery from weak 2009 usage levels in Japan, the European Union (EU), and the United States.  During the first half of 2010, world apparent usage grew by 7.3% (664,000 t) compared with that in the first half of 2009. Usage grew by 1.8% in China*, 11.7% in the EU, 37% in Japan and 4.9% in the United States.  Combined, these four regions currently account for 71% of total world refined copper usage. 

World mine production in the first half of 2010 remained practically unchanged compared with that in the first half of 2009 (+0.6%). Concentrate production grew by 0.4% while solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) grew by 1.4%. Production in Chile was up slightly (1.6%) from its low level during the first half of 2009, but output from other major producers such as Peru, the United States, Australia and Indonesia decreased by an aggregated 8% (-175,000t).  These four countries represent around 25% of total world copper mine production.  Mine production capacity utilization rates in the first half of 2010 were around 79%. 

During the first half of 2010, world refined production increased by 5.7% (508,000 t) compared with production in the same period of 2009: primary production increased by 2.2%, while secondary production (from scrap) increased by 26%. Note that the large relative increase in secondary refined copper production reflects in part the lower copper prices and consequent tight scrap market that existed in early 2009. World growth has been mainly driven by China (16.4%), Japan (12.4%) and the EU (10.2%) that combined represent almost one half of world refined copper production. Production in two other major world producers, Chile and the United States, which account for about one quarter of world production, decreased by a combined 2.3%. The refined production capacity utilization rate in the first half of 2010 increased to almost 80% from 77% in the same perio

d of 2009 and reflects increased scrap availability and the restoration of temporary cuts made in early 2009. The average LME cash price for August 2010 was US$ 7,283.95 per tonne, up from the July 2010 average of US$ 6,735.25 per tonne. The 2010 high and low copper prices through the end of August were US$7,950.50 and US$6,091.00 per tonne, respectively, and the average was US$7,097.45 per tonne. As of the end of August 2010, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 595,853 t, a decrease of 91,838 t from stocks held at the end of December 2009. Compared with the July levels, stocks were down at COMEX and LME and up at SHFE.
